newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks close at another record high.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks close at another record high.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 92.180 -0.085 Gold NY 340.55 Lon fix 342.80
*Stocks hit another record high close as bank shares continue to firm on higher dividend hopes. Vol 401.27 million, value A$955.38 million, 1,086 stocks traded, 313 steady, 401 up, 372 down.
The Australian share market ended at its second successive record closing high on Wednesday.
Banks sgare continued their recent strong run as investors tipped higher dividends ahead of the latest round of results.
At 4.20 p.m. (0620 GMT), the All Ordinaries index ended 4.8 points up at 2,517.6, building on Tuesday's record finish.
However, the June share price index futures defied the rise in the physical market, falling eight points to 2521 and narrowing the premium to the All Ords to 4.2 points.
Brokers said the fall in the futures and weaker bonds point to a possible drop in the All Ordinaries on Thursday.
Brokers said the fresh record high set on Wall Street underpinned the market rise, despite a shaky start.
"The consistency in the Dow is giving our market consistency. It is not being generated by us, it is coming from overseas," said Andrew Sekely, head of equities at Intersuisse.
Brokers said banks were finding good support and ignored the fall in the bond market.
Oil group Woodside was the strongest riser amongst the blue chips on vague rumours that its major shareholder Shell/Royal Dutch Group was going to buy the rest of the group out, brokers said.

Market heavyweight BHP saw the largest value of trade with about A$174 million going through the market or just under 20 percent of total market trading value, the buying interest helped the group recover some recent losses.
John Fairfax shares fell as rumours of a quick takeover for the newspaper group waned on political opposition to a bid for the publisher, particularly from Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting.
Base metals miner Pasminco attracted buying after its Century Zinc project got the go-ahead. Pasminco has agreed to buy to the project from RTZ-CRA.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trading was volatile as the SPI swung between positive and negative territory.
Contracts traded 7,788 (12,816)
Options trading was also active, but down on yesterday.
Total options traded 48,228 (57,266).
In other market news, Australian bond yields closed higher as the market braced for two key events on Thursday -- RBA governor Ian Mcfarlane testimony to parliament amd the April labour force report.
By 5.10 p.m. (0710 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.80 percent down eight basis points.
The Australian dollar ended with widespread losses but did recover from early lows in a seesaw session with heavy two-way flows. At 5.15 p.m. (0715 GMT), the dollar was trading at US$0.7750/55.
